name: EverMemOS

paper.title: EverMemOS: A Self-Organizing Memory Operating System for Structured Long-Horizon Reasoning

construction.unit: MemCell: Episode, Atomic Facts, Foresight, Metadata
construction.kept_as: rewritten third-person episode narrative + extracted atomic facts
construction.processing: LLM boundary detection at topic shifts; rewrite episode; derive facts and time-bounded foresight

organization.structure: MemCells clustered into thematic MemScenes + user profile
organization.stores: MemScene pool of MemCells; user profile (explicit facts, implicit traits)
organization.index: Qwen3-Embedding-4B dense + BM25 over atomic facts; scene centroids

management.operations: assimilate MemCell into nearest MemScene (sim > tau) or create new; refresh scene summary and profile
management.conflicts: profile updated from scene summaries with recency-aware updates and conflict tracking

retrieval.query: question; LLM writes 2-3 follow-up queries if context insufficient
retrieval.candidates: dense + BM25 fused by RRF over atomic facts; top N=10 MemScenes by max MemCell score
retrieval.selection: Qwen3-Reranker-4B reranks pooled episodes, keep K=10; LLM sufficiency check
retrieval.budget: N=10 scenes, K=10 episodes (~2.3-2.5k tokens on LoCoMo)

use.context: retrieved Episodes only (reasoning mode); chat mode adds profile and time-valid foresight
use.reasoning: single answer call after up to two retrieval rounds

classify.note: The reranker fixes the set; the LLM sufficiency check only decides whether to retrieve again.

stages.ingestion: An LLM-prompted Semantic Boundary Detector runs over a sliding window of the dialogue stream and cuts it into episode histories at topic shifts.
stages.construction: Each episode history is rewritten into a third-person Episode narrative (coreferences resolved), from which the LLM derives Atomic Facts and time-bounded Foresight signals with validity intervals; these plus metadata form a MemCell.
stages.organization: MemCells are incrementally clustered into thematic MemScenes (embedding similarity to scene centroid above threshold tau, with a max time-gap constraint); a user profile of explicit facts and implicit traits sits alongside.
stages.update: When a MemCell joins a MemScene the scene summary is updated and the user profile is refreshed from scene summaries with recency-aware updates and conflict tracking.
stages.retrieval: Dense (Qwen3-Embedding-4B) + BM25 over Atomic Facts fused by RRF; MemScenes scored by max member relevance (top N=10), Episodes pooled and re-ranked (Qwen3-Reranker-4B, K=10); an LLM sufficiency check triggers query rewriting (2-3 follow-up queries) when context is insufficient.
stages.answer: Reasoning mode answers from retrieved Episodes only; Chat mode additionally adds the User Profile and time-valid Foresight.

summary: Engram-inspired memory lifecycle: dialogue is segmented into MemCells (episode narrative, atomic facts, time-bounded foresight), clustered online into MemScenes with a user profile, and recalled via scene-guided agentic retrieval with a sufficiency check.
notes:
AXES-CHECK: selection is broader than 'Emb-4B + BM25 + Reranker-4B' - retrieval is scene-guided (MemScene scored by max MemCell relevance) and includes an LLM sufficiency verifier with query rewriting (second round triggered for 31.0% of LoCoMo questions, App. A.1). Dense+BM25 run over Atomic Facts, reranker over Episodes. Venue: ACL 2026 long paper (aclanthology 2026.acl-long.2125); ACL version gives code URL https://github.com/EverMind-AI/EverOS. Text read from the HF paper.md mirror of the arXiv paper (matches the ACL abstract).
DESIGN: Sec 3.2-3.5, 4.1, App. A.1, A.3, C.1. Corrected prefill: 'MemScene consolidation' moved from construction.processing to management.operations; retrieval selection split into candidates (Emb-4B+BM25) and selection (Reranker-4B + sufficiency check). Foresight expiry is a retrieval-time filter, not deletion, so forgetting=null. control.management=fixed-rule for threshold clustering (profile refresh itself is a prompted LLM).

sources.code_note: Commit 99aa0cad (2026-03-15, PR #134) adds scene retrieval; its comments cite 93% on LoCoMo, so it is taken as the evaluation code behind the paper's numbers. It is two months after paper v2, and the current repo (renamed EverOS) restarted its history in 2026-06, so exact identity with the paper's runs is not guaranteed.

glance.a: A MemCell: one topic segment of the dialogue, rewritten by an LLM into a third-person episode, plus atomic facts and time-bounded foresight.
Rewritten rather than cut to a fixed ratio: the prompt asks for a narrative of similar or shorter length. The raw turns are stored but never read.
MemCells are clustered into MemScenes by embedding similarity (τ 0.70 on LoCoMo) and a maximum time gap (7 days).
Yes. Qwen3-Reranker-4B scores the question against the episode text only and keeps 10.

glance.q: Is memory reconstructed at question time?
glance.a: Yes, when an LLM check finds the 10 episodes insufficient (31% of LoCoMo questions): it writes 3 new queries, searches all MemCells without scenes, and reranks up to 40 candidates again.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: Always 10 rewritten episodes, as "subject: episode", whether or not reconstruction ran. The original dialogue, atomic facts, profile and foresight are not included.

flow.title: Find matching MemCells
flow.out: up to 100 MemCells, one ranked list
flow.sees: Question vs each MemCell's atomic facts, subject and the first 200 characters of its episode (the paper says atomic facts only). Question and MemCell are embedded separately and compared by similarity; they never see each other.
flow.src: scene_retrieval.py L150-L157; stage2 L90-L160; config.py L57-L59

flow.title: Pick 10 MemScenes
flow.method: rule: a scene scores the best score among its MemCells (MaxSim)
flow.sees: Walks the ranked list from the top, noting each MemCell's scene, until 10 different scenes are covered. Scene summaries and centroids are not compared with the question.

flow.title: Gather every MemCell in those scenes
flow.method: rule: expand each scene to all its members
flow.out: their MemCells, e.g. 31 in the paper's trace
flow.sees: Every member joins, including MemCells that did not match the question. All start with the same score (1.0): the step-1 scores are dropped.

flow.title: Rerank and keep 10
flow.sees: One input per candidate: an instruction, the question and one episode text, read together. The model answers "yes" or "no" and the probability of "yes" is the score. Candidates never see each other (batches of 10 are only for speed). Subject, date and atomic facts are not shown. If fewer than 30% of batches succeed, the original order is used instead.

params.instruction: "contains specific facts, entities or details that directly answer the question"

flow.src: stage3 L82-L217; rerank_vllm.py L60-L80; config.py L73

flow.title: Is this enough to answer?
flow.out: sufficient, or a list of what is missing
flow.sees: The 10 episodes as Title / Date / Content (content cut at 500 characters) and the question. Returns sufficient or not, the key information found and the information still missing.
flow.yes: 69% of LoCoMo questions: answer with these 10 (step 10).
flow.src: scene_retrieval.py L247-L276; agentic_utils.py L184-L241; paper App. A.1

flow.title: Write new queries
flow.sees: The original question, the 10 round-1 episodes, the key information found and the missing information. It writes queries aimed at what is missing.

flow.title: Search all MemCells again
flow.method: bi-encoder (dense) + lexical (BM25) per query, fused by RRF, then the queries fused by RRF
flow.sees: Each new query searches every MemCell, not only the 10 scenes: scenes are not used in this round.

flow.title: Merge with round 1
flow.method: rule: round-1 results first, then new ones not already there
flow.sees: The round-1 10 are kept, then filled with new candidates up to 40.

flow.title: Rerank again and keep 10
flow.sees: Scored against the original question, not the new queries. There is no second sufficiency check: this is the last round.

flow.title: Answer
flow.model: the evaluated answer model (GPT-4.1-mini or GPT-4o-mini in the paper)
flow.sees: The 10 episodes as "subject: episode" under one header. No original dialogue, atomic facts, dates as a field, profile or foresight.

discussion.takeaway: Store memory as rewritten episodes grouped by theme, and read it with a rerank-then-check loop. In its own paper this gives the best LoCoMo and LongMemEval scores, with the largest gains on multi-hop and temporal questions.

claims.claim: Memory should be a lifecycle (form episodes, consolidate them into themes and a profile, reconstruct at question time), not a store of isolated records.
State of the art on memory-augmented reasoning.
claims.evidence: LoCoMo +9.2% (GPT-4.1-mini) and +7.0% (GPT-4o-mini) over Zep; LongMemEval +6.7% over MemOS. Table 1-2, §4.2

claims.claim: Grouping MemCells into scenes helps questions that need scattered evidence.
claims.evidence: LoCoMo multi-hop +19.7%, temporal +10.0%; LongMemEval knowledge update +20.6%. §4.2
Without MemScene 89.16, without MemCell 81.82, full 93.05 on LoCoMo. Fig. 4

claims.claim: The consolidated user profile adds signal beyond episodes.
claims.evidence: PersonaMem-v2: 53.25 with profile vs 43.93 episodes only. Table 4, §4.5

limits: LLM calls in construction and retrieval add latency and cost over single-pass baselines.
Current benchmarks cannot stress-test very long timelines.
reading: Scene summaries and the profile never reach the answer model in the scored runs, so the MemScene gain may come from widening the rerank pool rather than from narrative grouping; the ablation cannot tell these apart.
Round 2 (31% of questions) searches without scenes, and the paper's own trace example finds its answer there.
On LongMemEval a scene holds 1.36 MemCells on average, so the hierarchy is nearly flat.
Scene thresholds are set per dataset (0.70 and 7 days on LoCoMo, 0.50 and 30 days on LongMemEval).
Other papers report 85.5 to 94.5 for EverMemOS on LoCoMo; the answer model and judge differ, so the headline 93.05 is one setting.

abstract.text: EverMemOS treats long-term memory for LLM agents as a lifecycle rather than a pile of stored snippets. Dialogue is cut into topic segments and rewritten as MemCells (an episode, atomic facts and time-bounded plans), which are grouped into thematic MemScenes that also update a user profile. At question time the system opens the scenes that hold the best-matching MemCells, reranks their episodes, and searches again when an LLM judges the evidence insufficient. The authors report state-of-the-art results on LoCoMo, LongMemEval and PersonaMem-v2.
